'''Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli''' (5 November 1906 – 17 December 1981) was a Pakistani civil servant, Urdu poet, novelist, and filmmaker.<ref name=Gazdar/><ref name=ExpressNews/> 

He held positions in the prestigious [[Indian Civil Service]] before and after the partition of India.<ref name=DawnNews/> Following his retirement from public service in 1959, he embarked on a full-time career in filmmaking, contributing significantly to both Urdu literature and early Pakistani cinema.<ref name=Gazdar/><ref name=DawnNews/> 

Throughout his multifaceted career, he made significant contributions to literature and cinema, spanning British India and post-partition Pakistan. For example, his first film in Pakistan [[Chiragh Jalta Raha]] (1962) helped boost careers of [[Zeba (actress, born 1945)|Zeba]], [[Mohammad Ali (actor)|Mohammad Ali]] and [[Deeba]] in the [[Pakistani film industry]].<ref name=Gazdar/><ref name=DawnNews/>

== Early life and education ==
Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli was born on 5 November 1906, in [[Azamgarh]],<ref name=DawnNews/> in what was then the [[United Provinces of Agra and Oudh|United Provinces]] of [[Presidencies and provinces of British India|British India]].<ref name=DawnNews/> He completed his early education in [[Allahabad]] before traveling to England for higher studies at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]].<ref name=ExpressNews/> It was during his training for the Indian Civil Service (ICS) in [[England]] that he developed a keen interest in cinema, particularly the introduction of sound in films. He recognized the immense potential of film as a medium to convey messages to the masses, a passion that would later drive his filmmaking career.<ref name=DawnNews/>

== Career ==
After finishing his studies in England, upon his return to India, Fazli joined the [[Indian Civil Service]] and was appointed to various significant governmental roles in [[Bengal]].<ref name=DawnNews/> Fazli's passion for cinema, cultivated during his time in [[England]], led him to become a pioneer in the film industries of both pre-partition [[British India]] and post-partition [[Pakistan]].<ref name=DawnNews/> 

Fazli wrote extensively in Urdu under the pen name "Fazli," leaving behind a legacy of both poetry and prose.<ref name=ExpressNews/> He published his poetry collections include ''Naghma-e-Zindagi'' (1941).<ref name=ExpressNews/>

He was inspired by his older brothers, including S.F. Hasnain and Sibtain Fazli, to enter the film industry.<ref name=ExpressNews/> The Fazli brothers' 1938 film ''Qaidi'', which was released in 1940, is credited with pioneering the "Muslim Social" genre in undivided India.<ref name=DawnNews/> He later co-founded Fazli Brothers Ltd. in 1940. Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli also wrote the story for the 1942 film ''Masoom''.<ref name=DawnNews/>

Following the partition of [[India]] in 1947, Fazli migrated to the newly formed state of Pakistan and continued his public service career.<ref name=ExpressNews/> His notable roles included serving as Secretary for the Education Department in East Pakistan and as Secretary for the Ministry of Kashmir Affairs.<ref name=DawnNews/> In 1951, Fazli was invited by the U.S. government to deliver a series of guest lectures at American universities.<ref name=ExpressNews/> His civil service career concluded when he was "forcefully retired" in 1959, an event that led him to pursue filmmaking full-time.<ref name=DawnNews>{{cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1720671|title=FLASHBACK: LIGHTING THE PATH FOR OTHERS (Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli profile)|newspaper=Dawn newspaper|date=13 November 2022|url-status=dead|author=Muhammad Suhayb|archive-date=26 November 2022|access-date=1 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126042135/https://www.dawn.com/news/1720671}}</ref>

He continued writing under his pen name "Fazli" and wrote ''Chashm-e-Ghazaal'' (1953).<ref name=DawnNews/> After his retirement from civil service, he established his own production company, Dabistan Mehdood, in 1959. His most notable film was ''[[Chiragh Jalta Raha]]'' (1962), which he produced, wrote, and directed.<ref name=DawnNews/>

He hired famous singers [[Iqbal Bano]], [[Kajjan Begum]], [[Noor Jehan|Madam Noor Jehan]], M. Kaleem, Shabana. Indian playback singer [[Talat Mahmood]] was convinced by Fazli to sing three songs during his visit to [[Karachi]] to sing songs in his film ''Chiragh Jalta Raha''.<ref name=DawnNews/> The music was composed by Nihal Abdullah and included a famous folk wedding song originally written by the poet Amir Khusrau. The soundtrack, which included 14 songs in total, featured lyrics drawn from the poetry of literary figures such as [[Ghalib|Mirza Ghalib]], [[Mir Taqi Mir]], [[Jigar Moradabadi]], [[Mahir ul Qadri]] and [[Amir Khusro]], with Fazli also contributing to the lyrics.<ref name=DawnNews/>

The film was an adaptation of [[Oliver Goldsmith]]'s [[The Vicar of Wakefield]] and is notable for introducing several new talents, including actors [[Zeba (actress, born 1945)|Zeba]], [[Deeba]] and [[Mohammad Ali (actor)|Mohammad Ali]].<ref name=ExpressNews/> It premiered with [[Fatima Jinnah]] as the chief guest and won him a Nigar Award for best scriptwriter.<ref name=DawnNews/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehotspotonline.com/moviespot/bolly/Lollywood/NigarAwards.htm|date=17 June 2002|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 July 2008|title=The Nigar Awards (1957 - 1971)|website=The Hot Spot Online website|access-date=1 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080724022517/http://www.thehotspotonline.com/moviespot/bolly/Lollywood/NigarAwards.htm}}</ref>

He also produced, wrote, and directed ''Aisa Bhi Hota Hai'' (1965) and ''Waqt Ki Pukar'' (1967).<ref>{{cite book|last=Gazdar|first=Mushtaq|author-link=Mushtaq Gazdar|year=1997|title=Pakistan Cinema, 1947-1997|publisher=Oxford University Press via Google Books|page=258|isbn=0-19-577817-0}}</ref><ref name=Gazdar>{{cite book|last=Gazdar|first=Mushtaq|author-link=Mushtaq Gazdar|year=1997 |title=Pakistan Cinema, 1947-1997 - Chiragh Jalta Raha (1962 film)|publisher=Oxford University Press via Google Books|url=https://lib.zu.edu.pk/ebookdata/Media%20Sciences/Film/Pakistan%20Cinema%201947-1997%20by%20Mushtaq%20Gazdar.pdf|archive-date=9 September 2025|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250909185946/https://lib.zu.edu.pk/ebookdata/Media%20Sciences/Film/Pakistan%20Cinema%201947-1997%20by%20Mushtaq%20Gazdar.pdf|page=94|isbn=0-19-577817-0}}</ref><ref name=DawnNews/> His ghazals are characterized by a blend of classical style and modernist sensibility. He is also the author of the novels ''Khoon-e-Jigar Hone Tak'' and ''Sehar Hone Tak''. His book ''Pakistani Saqafat Wa Wataniyyat Ke Chand Pahlu'', which addressed national and patriotic issues, was published in 1970.<ref name=ExpressNews/>

== Personal life ==
Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli was known for his warmth and was affectionately called "Chacha Abba" by his family and close associates.<ref name=DawnNews/> He was part of a large family with several siblings who were also involved in the film industry.<ref name=DawnNews/> His son, Saeed Karim Fazli, followed in his footsteps as a film director and his grandson, Umair S. Fazli, has also contributed to cinema.<ref name=DawnNews/>

== Death ==
Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli died on December 17, 1981, in [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]], at the age of 75.<ref name=ExpressNews>{{cite web|url=https://www.express.pk/story/2427319/1|title=فضل احمد کریم فضلی مرحوم - Profile of Fazal Ahmad Karim Fazli|author=Sirajuddin Kazi|website=Express News|date=15 January 2023|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 February 2023|access-date=1 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203235529/https://www.express.pk/story/2427319/1/}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Fazli's work in film focused on patriotic and social themes, prioritizing meaningful content. Along with his brothers, Fazli is credited with pioneering the "Muslim Social" genre in pre-partition Indian cinema with the film ''Qaidi'' (1938).<ref name=ExpressNews/> This genre focused on social issues within Muslim families, and Fazli himself contributed the story for the brothers' subsequent film, ''Masoom'' (1942).<ref name=DawnNews/>

His 1962 film ''[[Chiragh Jalta Raha]]'' is particularly remembered for introducing several actors who would become legends in Pakistani cinema, including [[Zeba (actress, born 1945)|Zeba]], [[Mohammad Ali (actor)|Mohammad Ali]], [[Deeba]], [[Kemal Irani]] and [[Talat Hussain (actor)|Talat Hussain]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Gazdar |first=Mushtaq |author-link=Mushtaq Gazdar|year=1997|title=Pakistan Cinema, 1947-1997 |publisher=Oxford University Press via Google Books|page=250 |isbn=0-19-577817-0}}</ref><ref name=ExpressNews/> The film's premiere was even attended by Fatima Jinnah, signaling its cultural importance.<ref name=ExpressNews/><ref>{{cite book |last=Gazdar |first=Mushtaq |author-link=Mushtaq Gazdar |year=1997 |title=Pakistan Cinema, 1947-1997 |publisher=Oxford University Press |page=94 |isbn=0-19-577817-0}}</ref>
